rows.notes: Linear in log-odds. Strong baseline on tabular medical data; transparent + interpretable.
Greedy split on Gini/entropy. Single-tree overfits — Random Forest fixes it. Architect-friendly because every split is auditable.
rows.reference: McKinney 2017 · architect SRH Decision Trees PDF

rows.notes: 500-tree bagged ensemble. Robust on tabular; the 2024 medical-ML default.
Kernel-trick decision boundary. Excellent on small-to-medium tabular with non-linear structure.
Instance-based. Performance hinges on distance metric + feature scaling.
Unsupervised — clusters latent patient phenotypes. We report NMI 0.42 on heart-disease since accuracy is not directly defined.
rows.reference: McKinney 2017 ch. 10 · architect SRH Kmeans PDF

rows.notes: Assumes feature independence. Surprisingly strong on tabular when the features are roughly conditionally independent.
ReLU + softmax, 64-32 hidden. Marginal lift over LR on small tabular; shines as the dataset grows.
rows.reference: Raschka 2024 · architect SRH Neural Networks PDF

rows.notes: Sequence model. Not applicable to static tabular; reserved for vital-sign timelines + clinical narratives.
Multi-agent cascade: triage → specialist + diagnostic → validator → safety → privacy. Includes spreading-activation KG priors + sequential error-boost residuals.
Closed-source clinical LLM — current published USMLE-style state of the art.
8b biomedical fine-tune. Mörbius uses this as one of the HF fallback backends.
